prose: Krebs on Security: Microsoft's September Patch Tuesday fixes at least 974 vulnerabilities - by far its largest batch ever, obliterating July's record of 570 and pushing 2026 past 2,600 CVEs, more than double the previous record year. Two zero-days are being actively exploited (both privilege escalation), 113 bugs are critical, including a wormable DNS flaw (CVE-2026-69730) and a 9.8 CVSS Windows Shell RCE (CVE-2026-69829).

Microsoft credits AI-assisted discovery for the accelerating find rate, and it's not alone - Adobe, Cisco, Google, Mozilla and Oracle all report the same, with Google moving to security updates every two weeks. Experts' caveats: Tenable's Satnam Narang says AI is 'creating larger haystacks, not finding more needles' - organizations must prioritize by actual reachability; and Fortra's Tyler Reguly warns the human side (testing and deploying) is now the bottleneck, telling CISOs to budget dinners for weekend patching teams.
highlights: September Patch Tuesday: 974+ fixes, Microsoft's biggest batch ever
2026 already tops 2,600 CVEs - double the previous record year
Two exploited zero-days; 113 critical, incl. wormable DNS and a 9.8 Shell RCE
AI-assisted discovery credited industry-wide; Google moves to biweekly updates
Tenable: 'larger haystacks, not more needles' - prioritize by exploitability
The bottleneck is now human: testing and deploying the flood
